newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Pharmacia aims to speed discovery.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Pharmacia aims to speed discovery.

text.p: Pharmacia & Upjohn Inc said on Wednesday its research and development reorganisation was aimed at simplifying and speeding up the way decisions on drug development were made.
In a telephone interview with Reuters, Goran Ando, president of research and development, said the changes would allow the company "to reach decisions very fast."

"I am very confident that what we have brought out now is a very efficient organisation. Streamlined and very clear accountability will follow and give us an opportunity to enhance efficiency," he said.

The principal change announced on Wednesday was the replacement of three separate research and development structures based around Kalamazoo in the U.S, Stockholm in Sweden and Milan in Italy with single teams that will co-ordinate work across all three centres.
Ando said a small group of decision-making bodies based out of London would be in a better position to integrate the research and development operations with marketing and production.
"When a decision has been made by senior management we can carry it out very quickly," he said.
A major focus will be on improving co-ordination between Pharmacia's drug research activities and subsequent development through animal and human trials.
He said the structure "would help to define compounds in research and get them into development as soon as possible and prove the concept in man."
Ando said this was the point at which most drug projects failed. "It is very important to kill off non-performing projects very fast," he said.
The project will also aim to improve the link between the choice of drug projects and the company's marketing arm.
"It is important we don't do research for fun," Ando said.
The restructuring is the latest in a string of changes since Fred Hassan became Pharmacia & Upjohn's president and chief executive officer in May.
Ando said Hassan, who joined the company from American Home Products Corp, had influenced the global nature of the structure.
However he said the decision on R&D did not reflect serious problems with this part of the company, which has been rocked by a series of profit warnings and downgrades since it was formed.

"Overall if I look back on R&D over the past 18 months since merger we have got a lot to be proud of, because we have had a large number of filings, many approvals on time and a good flow of new drugs from research," Ando told Reuters.
